summary: Zstandard can use different window sizes, which limit memory use during compression and decompression. Some browsers cap the window size, which causes interoperability trouble. This document turns the recommended limit from RFC 8878 into a requirement for HTTP content encoding.

plainLanguage.summary: Zstandard uses a window size that affects memory use during decompression. This RFC sets an 8 MB limit for HTTP encoding and decoding to improve interoperability.

subtitle: Sets an 8 MB maximum Zstandard window size for HTTP content coding.

tldr.problem: Different decoder limits for Zstandard window sizes can make an HTTP response fail to decode.
tldr.mechanism: For zstd HTTP content coding, decoders must support windows up to 8 MB and encoders must not produce frames requiring larger windows.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9659 updates RFC 8878, turning its recommended 8 MB limit into an HTTP requirement.

today: RFC 9659 is an Informational document that updates RFC 8878. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Window Size Affects Interoperability
sections.content:
Zstandard, or zstd, is a lossless compression mechanism. In HTTP, the zstd content coding token signals that the content is Zstandard-compressed.

The Window_Size is the maximum distance for back-references and determines how much content must be kept in memory during decompression. Larger windows tend to improve compression ratio but use more memory; some browsers and user agents cap the size they will handle.
sections.plainLanguage: The window size controls how much memory a decoder needs. If the sender uses a larger window than the receiver accepts, the response may fail to decode.

sections.title: The 8 MB Limit
sections.content:
RFC 8878 recommends support for a Window_Size up to 8 MB and recommends that encoders not exceed it, but it does not impose requirements. RFC 9659 makes the limit mandatory when using the zstd HTTP content coding.

Decoders must support a Window_Size up to and including 8 MB. Encoders must not generate frames requiring more than 8 MB.
sections.plainLanguage: Decoders must handle a window up to 8 MB. Encoders must stay at or below that limit.

sections.title: Invalid Frames and Registry Update
sections.content:
The document introduces no new security considerations beyond RFC 8878. Decoders still need to handle oversized frames that do not follow the limit and fail decoding when they receive such invalid frames.

IANA updated the HTTP Content Coding Registry entry for zstd to describe the maximum Window_Size as 8 MB and cite this RFC and RFC 8878.
sections.plainLanguage: A decoder must still reject an oversized frame. The IANA entry now records the 8 MB requirement.
